messages:
Mira Chen: heads-up, noticed a drop in tokens_saved for a small set of customers starting ~03:10 UTC. dashboard spike looks like a regression.
Samir Patel: saw that too. Query in the new 'PK cache metrics' panel shows total tokens_saved down ~22% for model-phi on routes /chat/* for customer group B.
Alex Johnson: ops-bot just fired a perf-alert earlier: `prefetch_hitrate < 0.15 for model-phi` on box gp-7b-04. Link: https://graf.redwood/obs/d/pxk
Elena Rios: did we roll key-normalization last night? I remember a change to trim and lower-case prompt keys to reduce cardinality.
Samir Patel: yes, deploy at 23:45 PDST. The change canonicalizes whitespace and removes trailing control chars. It increased aggregation for many customers but could have broken some signature-based keys.
Mira Chen: hypothesis: we over-normalized tokens used in multipart prompts (customer B uses special separators). That makes the stored KV prefix mismatched because runtime hashing uses raw bytes for fast lookup.
Tyler K.: profiler shows increased KV lookup misses on the hot path and more small-batch inference calls -> kernel selection shifted toward lower-seq kernels, increasing per-token overhead.
Alex Johnson: here's the trace snippet from the runtime logs:
```
[2026-03-18T03:09:02Z] serve.request id=abcd kv_lookup=false key_raw="\x1fuser:sep|..." key_norm="user:sep|..." fallback_model=model-phi
[2026-03-18T03:09:02Z] kernel.select name=attn_small seq=48 batch=1
```
Elena Rios: interesting that key_raw contains control chars; normalization removed them which changed the KV key. For some customers their client intentionally includes those chars for delimiting metadata.
Mira Chen: action: revert whitespace normalization for keys until we implement a safe canonicalization that preserves delimiter bytes. Can someone own an immediate rollback? @Alex
Alex Johnson: I can roll back the normalization flag for runtime-only (non-storage) by 03:30. Will also add a quick A/B toggle so Dedicated customers can opt-in.
Samir Patel: in parallel I'll add a temporary dashboard panel breaking tokens_saved by key_version and by route/customer. New query:
```
sum(tokens_saved) by (model,route,customer,key_version)
```
so we can see which key_version lost value.
Tyler K.: also instrument kernel.choice and batch_size distribution on the same dashboard. If small batches increase we need to tweak batching heuristics back to prefer larger batch windows for legacy keys.
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2026-0318-01 (pk-keynorm-regression). Pager duty: eng-runtime on call.
Elena Rios: for warmup: we should update prefetch rules: add a fallback warmup pass that keys on raw and normalized variants for the first N tokens to populate both caches. That will avoid cold misses during rollouts.
Mira Chen: good idea. Add a regression test in perf-suite: generate multipart prompts with control delimiters and assert canonicalization preserves match for existing keys.
Samir Patel: TODOs:
- Alex: rollback normalization flag (in progress)
- Samir: add key_version panel + route/customer slice
- Tyler: batch distribution panel + tweak heuristics fallback
- Elena: prototype dual-warmup prefetch
- Mira: add perf-case to CI
Alex Johnson: rollback deployed at 03:28, monitoring now.
Mira Chen: looks like tokens_saved trending back up for affected customers in the dashboard. kernel.choice still skewed a bit but batch_size is recovering.
Samir Patel: closing loop: we'll keep the key_version panel for 48h, and plan an improved normalization approach that is delimiter-aware and has an explicit compatibility mode for legacy customers.
Tyler K.: filing a follow-up RFC for batching heuristics to handle key-version churn + kernel selection safety nets.
Elena Rios: thanks team. ops-bot, please post incident update when we hit stable for 1h.
ops-bot: incident INC-2026-0318-01 status -> mitigated, updated 03:57 UTC."
